item.text: {"question_id":"6B.5","answer":"During 2023, Mexico had substantial formal measurement, audit, and evaluation capacity, but the evidence supports only mixed executive correction of failure. CONEVAL reported publishing multidimensional poverty and social-rights indicators, coordinating 173 mandated evaluations, disseminating 95% of coordinated evaluations, and completing 95% of recorded improvement commitments; however, these are largely self-reported institutional outputs and do not establish that the president personally used findings or implemented recommendations (BATCH-0006-E003; BATCH-0013-E007; BATCH-0054-E007). The 2023 IMSS-BIENESTAR rules provided for supervision, performance and quality review, internal and external evaluation by recognized specialists or institutions, public reporting, audits, complaints, social auditing, and follow-up actions; they also specified 19 performance indicators. These provisions establish formal mechanisms, not their completed operation, independence, findings, or effectiveness (BATCH-0051-E004; BATCH-0051-E005; BATCH-0051-E006). Evidence of substantive correction is limited but not absent: CONEVAL reported that Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro improved some component design, and Sembrando Vida used local coordination and operational adjustments to address some plant-quality problems; these changes are not clearly attributable to a presidential decision or demonstrably tied to completed evaluation findings (BATCH-0052-E006; BATCH-0048-E009). Conversely, CONEVAL found that 3 of 16 priority programs lacked adequately defined target populations, 4 needed indicator adjustments, 4 did not measure results, 8 needed stronger logical links between components and objectives, and 2 lacked coverage indicators; it specifically reported that Universities for Wellbeing worsened from needing improvement in 2021 to having no results orientation in 2023, while Producción para el Bienestar worsened in logical association (BATCH-0052-E002; BATCH-0052-E006; BATCH-0052-E008). The health-access evidence also shows a major adverse outcome associated with the Seguro Popular-to-Insabi transition, including a rise in reported health-service-access deprivation from 16.2% in 2018 to 39.1% in 2022, while the source notes possible links to institutional transition, inadequate coordination, and lower proportional health spending without claiming a complete causal evaluation (BATCH-0032-E003). Segalmex audits and reporting identified extensive irregularities and missing documentation during 2019–2021; cooperation and corrective investigation followed under director Leonel Cota Montaño, but the supplied evidence does not establish presidential personal responsibility or successful resolution (BATCH-0007-E003; BATCH-0011-E001). Independent oversight was also qualified by reported nonoperation of mandated forensic-data institutions, opaque methodology and open-data gaps, and delayed appointments affecting autonomous bodies (BATCH-0018-E017; BATCH-0026-E014). Overall, credible measurement and formal avenues for audit and evaluation were well evidenced, but transparent, independent, timely, ruler-directed correction when programs failed was not consistently
